subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: Should OpenClaw promise an enforceable per-session private mode, and exactly which reads, writes, providers, tools, plugins, logs, and lifecycle events must that promise cover?
rationale: A privacy badge is a security promise; implementation cannot safely begin until maintainers choose the threat model, activation authority, persistence boundary, and behavior across restart and child-session flows.

options.title: Approve full private-session contract
options.body: Design an additive core mode with explicit guarantees and enforcement across every OpenClaw-owned context and persistence surface before exposing the UI toggle.

options.title: Limit scope to context suppression
options.body: Offer a clearly named demo-context mode that suppresses bootstrap injection but explicitly does not claim incognito or no-persistence guarantees.

options.title: Decline the mode
options.body: Keep existing contextInjection and cleanup controls, document their limitations, and avoid presenting them as a privacy guarantee.

recommendation.title: Approve full private-session contract
recommendation.body: Design an additive core mode with explicit guarantees and enforcement across every OpenClaw-owned context and persistence surface before exposing the UI toggle.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent canonical review and session-area history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product and security decision.
